title: Definability: parameters, symmetries, and what formulas can describe
summary: Describe subsets and function graphs by formulas, test definitions using symmetries, and count the limits of finite parameters.
abstract: Which subsets of a structure can its own formulas describe? In the real numbers with order alone, a formula can describe the points to the right of a chosen parameter, but cannot single out the positive numbers without naming where they begin. This difference leads to definability with and without parameters. A definable set must be preserved by every symmetry of the structure that fixes its parameters, giving a practical way to prove that no definition exists. The converse fails: even a structure with no nontrivial symmetries has undefinable subsets when its domain is infinite and its language is countable. Formulas describe only a limited part of the subsets available in the surrounding mathematics.
